takeaways: Start with out-of-the-box configuration and move to pro-code only when low-code is not enough, while keeping Dataverse security and governance in place.
Use Power Pages for external users on top of Dataverse, and secure the Web API with enabled fields, table permissions and column permissions instead of hiding data in the client.
AI speeds up prototypes and bug fixes, but developers remain responsible for review, security audits and spending tokens only where they create real impact.
hook: Low-code makes it easy to build apps and portals, and just as easy to expose data to the world by accident. In this conversation, Microsoft MVP Michel Mendes shares his path from SharePoint developer to Power Platform architect and explains how makers and architects can build Power Pages and Power Apps solutions that are secure, scalable and maintainable.
